recall_prompt: Say how you would find the conjugate of this quotient — what you do first, and what a conjugate changes.
insider_note: Simplify the quotient to a + ib first and only then flip the sign of the i part. Watch −5i² in the numerator: it is +5, and after cancelling 5 the number is (1 + 7i)/10 — the conjugate is then one sign change.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Simplify the quotient
steps.margin_note: First mark. Multiply above and below by 7 − i. The denominator becomes 49 + 1 = 50; the numerator 35i − 5i² = 5 + 35i.

recall.must_convey: That multiplying by the conjugate 7 − i simplifies the quotient to (1 + 7i)/10.
accept: multiply top and bottom by seven minus i, the bottom is fifty and the top is five plus thirty five i, so one plus seven i by ten
rationalise to get one plus seven i over ten
the quotient simplifies to one plus seven i by ten
conjugate seven minus i tho multiply cheste one plus seven i by ten vasthundi
five i into seven minus i over fifty, that is one plus seven i over ten

steps.why: The conjugate of a quotient must be taken after the quotient is a single a + ib; a complex denominator hides which part is imaginary. Multiplying by 7 − i makes the denominator real, and the common factor 5 cancels.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to cancel the 5, leaving (5 + 35i)/50 — not wrong, but the conjugate is easier to read from (1 + 7i)/10.

steps.label: Take the conjugate
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Keep the real part 1/10, flip the imaginary part.
lines: The conjugate of a + ib is a − ib.

recall.must_convey: That the conjugate changes the sign of the imaginary part, so the conjugate is (1 − 7i)/10.
accept: change the sign of the imaginary part, the conjugate is one minus seven i by ten
the answer is one minus seven i over ten
flip the sign of seven i to get one minus seven i by ten
imaginary part sign marchithe one minus seven i by ten
conjugate keeps one by ten and turns plus seven i into minus seven i

steps.why: Conjugation reflects the number in the real axis: the real part 1/10 stays, the imaginary part 7/10 becomes −7/10. The denominator 10 is real and is not touched.
common_mistakes: Changing the sign of the whole fraction to (−1 − 7i)/10.
Stopping at (1 + 7i)/10 without writing its conjugate.
